cases.purpose: banip/unbanip with an invalid IP or jail token is refused with an 'invalid' diagnostic (status 2) and changes no ban state
cases.oracle: fail2ban.c token rules (IPv4 ^[0-9]{1,3}(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}$, IPv6 hex with ':', jail ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$) and exit status 2 for invalid tokens; The frozen fail2ban builtin documents only parse-command/validate-ip/validate-jail/format-status/selftest (fail2ban.c header) and no mutation, firewall or daemon-client verb; this case states the documented fail2ban-client behavior (banip/unbanip/reload/status with -s SOCKET, ban.db as the DB operand like format-status) and records the candidate's reached failure. Any operand layout is rejected at the subcommand level, so the failure does not depend on the layout chosen.
cases.comparison: Status, an 'invalid' diagnostic and absence of any ban.db for three invalid requests.
cases.script:
[[ $UID == 2000 && $EUID == 2000 && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || exit 125
IFS= read -r marker </etc/bashos-parity-vm || exit 125
IFS= read -r vendor </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor || exit 125
[[ $vendor == QEMU && $marker =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$ ]] || exit 125
[[ $(type -t fail2ban) == builtin ]] || exit 125
b() { "$@" && echo 1 || echo 0; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p bin; printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "$@" >>"$HOME/fw.log"\n' >bin/fw; /usr/bin/chmod +x bin/fw; : >"$HOME/fw.log"
t() { local l=$1 out rc; shift; out=$("$@" 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "$l: rc=$rc diag-says-invalid=$([[ $out == *invalid* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0) db-exists=$([[ -e ban.db ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"; }
t bad-ip fail2ban banip ban.db sshd 1.2.3
t bad-jail fail2ban banip ban.db "bad jail" 192.0.2.1
t bad-unban-ip fail2ban unbanip ban.db sshd 12.34.56.7890
cases.stdout:
bad-ip: rc=2 diag-says-invalid=1 db-exists=0
bad-jail: rc=2 diag-says-invalid=1 db-exists=0
bad-unban-ip: rc=2 diag-says-invalid=1 db-exists=0

cases.purpose: banip appends <ip>\t<jail>\t<epoch> rows to an isolated ban.db, unbanip removes only the named row, status reflects each transition, and a mock firewall actor sees the requests
cases.oracle: fail2ban-client semantics and the ban.db row format in the fail2ban.c header; a mock fw executable that appends its argv to a private log; The frozen fail2ban builtin documents only parse-command/validate-ip/validate-jail/format-status/selftest (fail2ban.c header) and no mutation, firewall or daemon-client verb; this case states the documented fail2ban-client behavior (banip/unbanip/reload/status with -s SOCKET, ban.db as the DB operand like format-status) and records the candidate's reached failure. Any operand layout is rejected at the subcommand level, so the failure does not depend on the layout chosen.
cases.comparison: Return statuses, the exact ban.db rows with an epoch inside the sampled window, remaining rows after unbanip, format-status output after each step, and mock fw invocations naming the IP.
cases.script:
[[ $UID == 2000 && $EUID == 2000 && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || exit 125
IFS= read -r marker </etc/bashos-parity-vm || exit 125
IFS= read -r vendor </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor || exit 125
[[ $vendor == QEMU && $marker =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$ ]] || exit 125
[[ $(type -t fail2ban) == builtin ]] || exit 125
b() { "$@" && echo 1 || echo 0; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p bin; printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "$@" >>"$HOME/fw.log"\n' >bin/fw; /usr/bin/chmod +x bin/fw; : >"$HOME/fw.log"
t0=$(/usr/bin/date +%s)
export PATH=/tmp/parity-case/bin
fail2ban banip ban.db sshd 192.0.2.7; r1=$?
fail2ban banip ban.db sshd 192.0.2.8; r2=$?
fail2ban banip ban.db nginx 198.51.100.4; r3=$?
t1=$(/usr/bin/date +%s)
rows=0; ok=1
while IFS=$'\t' read -r ip jail ep; do rows=$((rows+1)); [[ -n $ip && -n $jail && $ep -ge $t0 && $ep -le $t1 ]] || ok=0; done <ban.db 2>/dev/null
echo "banip: rc=$r1,$r2,$r3 rows=$rows row-format-and-epoch-ok=$ok first=$(head -n1 ban.db 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/tr '\t' ' ' | /usr/bin/cut -d' ' -f1,2)"
st=$(fail2ban format-status ban.db sshd 2>&1)
echo "status-after-ban: both-ips=$([[ $st == *192.0.2.7* && $st == *192.0.2.8* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
fail2ban unbanip ban.db sshd 192.0.2.7; r4=$?
rows=0; left=; while IFS=$'\t' read -r ip jail ep; do rows=$((rows+1)); left="$left $ip/$jail"; done <ban.db 2>/dev/null
st=$(fail2ban format-status ban.db sshd 2>&1)
echo "unbanip: rc=$r4 rows=$rows left=[$left ] status-without-removed=$([[ $st == *192.0.2.8* && $st != *192.0.2.7* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
fw=$(<"$HOME/fw.log")
echo "mock-fw: mentions-ban-ip=$([[ $fw == *192.0.2.7* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0) calls=$(/usr/bin/wc -l <"$HOME/fw.log")"
cases.stdout:
banip: rc=0,0,0 rows=3 row-format-and-epoch-ok=1 first=192.0.2.7 sshd
status-after-ban: both-ips=1
unbanip: rc=0 rows=2 left=[ 192.0.2.8/sshd 198.51.100.4/nginx ] status-without-removed=1
mock-fw: mentions-ban-ip=1 calls=4

cases.purpose: The client sends reload and status over a private Unix control socket to a daemon and reports its reply; a reload reaches the firewall backend (mocked)
cases.oracle: A mock control daemon on a private Unix socket (helpers/mig-w6-f2b-mock.py) that records requests and returns a fixed jail status, plus a mock fw executable; The frozen fail2ban builtin documents only parse-command/validate-ip/validate-jail/format-status/selftest (fail2ban.c header) and no mutation, firewall or daemon-client verb; this case states the documented fail2ban-client behavior (banip/unbanip/reload/status with -s SOCKET, ban.db as the DB operand like format-status) and records the candidate's reached failure. Any operand layout is rejected at the subcommand level, so the failure does not depend on the layout chosen.
cases.comparison: Connections seen by the mock daemon, the verb in the request bytes, the client's stdout against the daemon reply and the mock firewall call, for reload and status.
cases.script:
[[ $UID == 2000 && $EUID == 2000 && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || exit 125
IFS= read -r marker </etc/bashos-parity-vm || exit 125
IFS= read -r vendor </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor || exit 125
[[ $vendor == QEMU && $marker =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$ ]] || exit 125
[[ $(type -t fail2ban) == builtin ]] || exit 125
b() { "$@" && echo 1 || echo 0; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p bin; printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "$@" >>"$HOME/fw.log"\n' >bin/fw; /usr/bin/chmod +x bin/fw; : >"$HOME/fw.log"
printf 'Status\n|- Number of jails:\t1\n`- Jail list:\tsshd\n' >reply.txt
MOCK=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w6-f2b-mock.py
mock() { # LABEL CLIENT-COMMAND
  /usr/bin/rm -f "$HOME/rep.json" "$HOME/out.txt" "$HOME/rc.txt"; : >"$HOME/fw.log"
  /usr/bin/python3 "$MOCK" /tmp/parity-case/f2b.sock reply.txt "$HOME/rep.json" -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "PATH=/tmp/parity-case/bin $2 >\"\$HOME/out.txt\" 2>/dev/null; echo \$? >\"\$HOME/rc.txt\""
  /usr/bin/python3 -I - "$1" <<'PY'
import json, sys
r = json.load(open("/tmp/parity-home/rep.json"))
rc = open("/tmp/parity-home/rc.txt").read().strip()
out = open("/tmp/parity-home/out.txt").read()
fw = open("/tmp/parity-home/fw.log").read()
print("%s: rc=%s connections=%d request-has-verb=%d stdout-equals-daemon-reply=%d fw-called=%d" % (
    sys.argv[1], rc, r["connections"], any(b"reload" in bytes.fromhex(x) or b"status" in bytes.fromhex(x) for x in r["requests"]),
    out == "Status\n|- Number of jails:\t1\n`- Jail list:\tsshd\n", bool(fw.strip())))
PY
}
mock reload "fail2ban -s /tmp/parity-case/f2b.sock reload"
mock status "fail2ban -s /tmp/parity-case/f2b.sock status"
cases.stdout:
reload: rc=0 connections=1 request-has-verb=1 stdout-equals-daemon-reply=0 fw-called=1
status: rc=0 connections=1 request-has-verb=1 stdout-equals-daemon-reply=1 fw-called=0
